The war is over but the world still moves on. Life at Empire City slowly but surely gets back on track. First order of business; rebuilding Hampstead. The speaker didn’t spend too much time here but a project such as rebuilding an entire borough would need all the help it can get. Amidst the rebuilding, the Speaker tries to pay as much homage and respect to the dead as he can.

    Amidst all the busywork, the Speaker manages to hangout with his friends in the city. He meditates in Murry Hill Park and helps with the Mender and Sabrine. He debates with Vivica Midask about philosophy and politics. And he reconnects with his first friend, Irynx. It was a long and arduous adventure to get to where they were now. Things between them will never be the same and that’s good. The Speaker has grown and matured and his relationships reflect this. Once naive and lost now wisened and hardened by loss.

    Irynx leaves their Airship, now christened as the Raven Queen, under the Speaker’s care. Ace Pilot Wings heavy in his pocket, the Speaker agrees gladly. He gives away his old airship and moves into the Queen. While remodeling and rearranging, the Speaker comes across a fairly surprising discovery. In a small crack by the airship walls lies an extradimensional captain’s quarters with none other but Meorys inside. Meorys was using some Nolzur’s Marvelous Pigments to counterfeit some coin, both continental currency and British pounds and stockpiling them in a box labeled ‘Just in case the revolution fails’. In her paranoia, Meorys has missed the revolution.

The Speaker bids farewell to all of his friends at the city and embarks on his first trip out of Arcania borders. He journeys south for Meorys’s hometown to drop her off there. Meorys tells the Speaker that they both came from here and that the Speaker was once a noble of this lands, the Faranells she said. The Speaker has no memories of this whatsoever but one this is for sure, the person that left this place for Empire city is no longer. That person died long ago and now the Speaker, a brand new person, stands in their place. Meorys and the Speaker bid each other farewell, marking the end to the Ball Eater crew.

    The Speaker embarks on his next adventure. Time to finish up his deal with a dragon. He lays out his tarot deck in front of him, the world card face up serving to strengthen his connection to the spirit world as he calls out for Nidhogg. Invoking the name of Nidhogg with the intention to speak with him gives the Speaker the feeling of his cold breath wrapping around your skin. A low growl rumbles against his chest, the dragon of Yggdrasil is listening.

The Speaker takes a deep breath to collect his thoughts. "The war against Britain is over, Arcania has won. Though I assume you already know this. I am here to hold up my end of the bargain. I am awaiting your orders." The Speaker speaks with forced politeness. "Cross you the eastern Ocean. Bring yourself to bear against my enemies, Ephemeral." The Speaker grins mentally. "Nice timing, I was about to go there myself." He then scolds himself as he regains seriousness. "Enemies? Odin?"

"The Aesir move against the once and future king. My people enslaved by the Hanging one, the one eyed God of Thieves and Heroes is bringing the berzerker rage against the Knights of the Round. The war is pitched and laying waste to all of the lands between them. Gods who call themselves good ignore the Gods who call themselves evil to make war against one another. And in the midst of these battles, Arthur's Dragon Merlin moves against my people. My servants among the living."

"And this is where I step in." The Speaker lets out a breath of relief. He was bracing himself for Nidhogg ordering him to do unspeakable atrocities, continuing the fight against Britain is no such thing. "Who am I fighting with? Is there a representative of your people I am to meet up with?"

"Saint George the Dragon Slayer is named among the great heroes of Britannia. Morgana Le fey would see Merlin destroyed. Aid her in this and then she shall aid you in the defeat of Saint George. Without his dragon lance, my people: the trolls, the dark elves, the giants shall no longer fear that Jörmungandr be slain."

The Speaker nods. "I understand. I will head out for Britain, seek out these people, and defeat the king's dragon. I shall do this to uphold our agreement and to help your people. Evil, good, or anything else I shall not let anyone be oppressed by the British no longer. I'll be meeting you once more after this is all over, in one way or another."

"You will not meet me again. You are my unshackling. You have bound yourself to my service. And that service extends into your death. At the time of your death, I will finally abdicate Hel and name you my successor. Foolish mortal. Your death will be an unending task of tending to the unwanted dead."

The Speaker flinches and nearly falls to the ground. This is the catch he's been expecting, but in all his wildest imaginations, this wasn't in them. He is speechless.

Nidhogg fades. His command is complete.

He remembers all he's been through to put him in this situation and regains his composure. He starts speaking to no one in particular. "As Speaker for the Dead, I accept this." Not like he had a choice. "Unwanted the souls under me may be, but voiceless they will not. I shall serve as a warning for those who unnecessarily give away parts of themselves. Those who purposely throw away themselves shall end up under the watch of the Nameless Speaker." 

With a heavy heart, the speaker sails for Britain.

The Speaker rounds up those not loyal to the crown, those who have a bone to settle with the monarchy. The frivolous behavior of the former King George saw to the Speaker seeing no shortage of able helpers. He calls on the help of a young inventor, a kenku priestess of a god of trickery, a shady gunslinger, a loxodon folk singer, and brutish barbarian. With a ramshackle crew under his command, the Speaker flies for Morgana Le Fey, sworn enemy to the dragon Merlin.

    Finding Morgana was easy enough, she wasn’t exactly subtle with her actions. Convincing her to join was the hard part. Morgana is a powerful sorceress, as stubborn as she is talented. She believed that no one was worthy to be deemed on her level and only she alone can take on the challenge of fighting Merlin. Fortunately, playing the role of one below another is something the Speaker is highly familiar with. With some clever words and silvered promises of a ship, Morgana Le Fey joins the crew of the Raven Queen. She grows tired of working in dingy castles and dungeons, a flying base of operations would be a much better replacement.

With his crew now assembled and a powerful sorceress at his side. Merlin’s time is coming to an end. The Raven Queen flies south, it flies for Wales.

    Without Morgana’s long accrued knowledge of Merlin and its weaknesses, the Speaker wouldn’t be able to take out the dragon and without the Speaker and his crew Morgana would’ve lacked the needed firepower and resilience to outmatch Merlin. It is only through their cooperation that Merin would fall. Through the help of the spirits and the brute strength of the nordic dead, Merlin is flushed out of his lair. Morgana’s magicks keep him distracted and bogged down while the artillery fire of the Raven Queen tears away at his defenses. Taking a page out of Captain Midask’s book on how to slay a dragon the Speaker constructs a volatile creation using the leftovers of Meorys’s pigments, tempered with the expertise of the mechanic onboard. With this ramshackle contraption of oil flasks and ball bearings, Merlin is laid to rest. The wings of Arthur fall and the forces of Odin descend upon the British isles. The speaker’s job isn’t over yet however, there is still one foe that stands between him and his duty. Saint George the Dragonslayer needs to be cast down.

content:
The fight with Merlin renders the Raven Queen grounded and its crew busy. The Speaker and Morgana alone face the saint. This battle plays out differently from the clash with Merlin. Without his ship around them, the Speaker and Morgana are vulnerable and Saint George proves to be a highly competent combatant. It is only through sheer luck and with the strength of spirits, quite literally, that the Speaker continues to fight. With berserkers surrounding him and Morgana’s magic manipulating the tides of the battle, Saint George is almost beaten, but his aim proves true and his dragonlance punches through dragon-like flesh as it skewers the Speaker. The Speaker doesn’t go without a fight however as a well time point blank shatter spell manages to break apart the lance of Saint George and renders him open towards Morgana’s attacks.

    Thus this is the end to the Speaker’s tale. A sorceress beside him, promising to take care of the airship and crew he leaves behind and finally giving it the proper chance to be more than just a vessel for war, a large hole in his chest letting out blood at an alarming rate, and no raven, fey, mad scientist, or mender in site to bring his spirit back. The Speaker’s eyes go dull and lifeless and his spirit goes straight down.

**Matteo and Despo:**
The inseparable pair of mice continued their work at the café before accepting the offer to be Awakened on April 22, 1779.

However, they did not stay at the café for long after their Awakening. Armed with their wits, their acts, and each other the pair made their way to Broadway. 

The pair did their best as actors among the scene but for all their heart and skill they were often typecast or used solely in narration roles due to their small stature. 

Undeterred from their struggles the pair worked more diligently and became playwrights and directors instead. And while their small size made it difficult for them as performers it became an unlikely asset in their new directions allowing them to give better presentations of what they are looking for during rehearsals and casting. And on more than one occasion dashing across stage to provide an understudy their lines should the actor freeze up during a performance.

As actors they were constantly told they had the gift, but as writers and directors they were able bring their dreams and acts succefully to the stage.

No one is quite sure what happened to the pair however. One day they simply vanished. However, on a rare occasion a new script is delivered, without any author or credentials, and yet these mysterious plays are often great successes for the directors bold enough to try and bring these plays to life.

Matteo and Despo's Bibliography includes:
A nine part series of plays of warrior monks far off in the Astral Sea, a harrowing tale of romance, betrayal, the strength of ones will, and a mysterious Force that flows through all things.

A three act play telling the tale of an cursed piece of jewelry and a group of heroes questing to destroy it, having many hardships and separations along the way.

A series of plays about a local legend, some titanic dinosaur that both causes destruction to the city, but also protects it from other titans.

A play about a minstrel that lives in the sewers that strikes ever couple decades, and a group of misfits that ends its terror.

And many many more.

Mictlan

Mictlan does not leave right away. They spend several more weeks in town, helping with the rebuilding efforts as best they can. Drop by the library a few times, scribbling fiercely as if their life depends on it. The time is used getting better at being in their own skin, settling in somewhere in the midst of their feathers and learning the art of a smile. 

At the end of the three weeks, they know they do not belong anymore. Mictlan could, if they really tried, but wanderlust has come with the snow-white feathers and they… they want to see. There are only so many years left in their life, after all, and so many places left in the world. 

Before they leave, Mictlan drops by Ferrytown. They greet the shifter children, smiling in only the way only they know how. Enter the herb shop, singing something high and melodious to the plants in Celestial with an underpinning of something deeper in the throat. It somehow still works.

They leave as suddenly as they entered, with a silver for the ferry and the plants glistening, watered. 

Eρευνα stands empty in the docks, waiting for its next owner. There’s a book hidden under a floorboard in there, words spaced between arcane sigils in a sort of a journal most cannot read. 

The shifter speaks with any they come across as they exit the city, because politeness dictates it. They are happy, but brief, and will not be stayed. 

A feathered silhouette passes through the land, carrying a bag and following the land due north-northeast. Their steps are light along the road, a familiar shape hovering behind Mictlan’s shoulder all eyes and feathers and rings. Just before they leave sight of the city they step forward and *changes* into something with a large wingspan, striking out with joyous beats of their wings. Their cousin-familiar (Aefirael) follows, spinning. 
** **

That’s not the last place they are spotted, but their movements become erratic over the years. Mictlan seems to go for knowledge and history, both in the past and that which will become it. They seem to seek out flight, but not too much after the first few years. 

(They do not make a deal with the fae, but do consider it the first couple of years. No, they decide later; The sky is missed, but even before they did not spend all day in the air.)

Mictlan never stays in once place for long. They do not quite revisit places, either, as far as can be told. Throughout the years they get better at magic as one must if they keep on that path, and perhaps they meet people they saw earlier in life. Find ways of extending their own life, as they suppose most mortals must go for once they see so much more that they can do. The celestial- or, well, not celestial anymore, not for a long time- writes it down in a growing spellbook and moves on.

They may only stay for the duration of their natural lifetime, but that had ended twice already before they even left the city. And yet, there is an acute sense of mortality. Attachments trail behind them like a path of stardust, some growing stronger and others tapering out. Age catches up to the best, unless it doesn’t.

Perhaps it takes only decades. Perhaps it takes lifetimes. But a feathered serpent loops around whatever the old city has become as they leave again for sights unseen and unknown. Once. Twice. Thrice, waving a scaled wing as it flies into the rising sun. Their cousin is not with them. 

It's taken them so many years, so many lifetimes, but at last they know where they’re going. 

Where they’ve always been going. 

Home. The long way round.
There we go!

__**LEAVING**__
"Do you still remember the times before we met each other?" Irynx asks the other people on the Strider.

Sabrine laughs. 'I mean… you're asking me, there wasn't exactly that much time. But yes, the times before, of fear and mistrust… I have to actively think to remember those now.'

Orphy sighs, adjusting the seat belts on a sleepy Corbianne. `Ah. The good old days, when our lives were constantly in danger! Wait, no. Empire City was worse, actually.`

Ed chuckles and mutters "What's life without a little danger?"

"Back in my home town it wasn't that bad," Roy says from the driver's seat, fiddling with some controls before they depart. "And arrival to the City was pretty bland and boring. Overall improvement from that, I suppose."

`I remember absolutely nothing!` Kukudh chimes in, sounding happier than they should about this. Sabrine looks to Roy, 'I'd still like to visit your hometown some time, if possible. Though I understand if you wouldn't want to.'

"Honestly…" Roy thinks for a moment. "I don't think going back to the old lands is a good idea anymore. My swarm did kinda send me here so I'm out of the way, and well, I haven't really fulfilled the task given to me. For one, I'm not expanding the swarm's influence, and then on top of that I kind of have my own separate swarm from my town's one. Which they should've expected, but not much of that plan was really planned."

Sabrine nods. 'Understandable.' `Hey, could always send me just to look around.` '…no, with that, I think best not. Same reasoning as, ah… earlier's moving on discussion.'

"Swarm," Cor murmurs, before Orphy soothes her back into a sleepy state.

"Alright, everyone seated or planted, and Grimmy ready to follow?" Roy says, doing a quick headcount over the seats behind him. "Let's roll, then. The west awaits."

__**WILLIAM**__
Orphy starts to fly around the strange tabaxi in a circle. Irynx is busy braiding flowers into her daughter's hair, but looks up to eye her familiar. "What are you doing? You're not a vulture."

`Shhh. I was just observing him.` Orphy lands on a branch in front of the tabaxi, beak uncomfortably close to his face. `So, William, right? You… have really great vibes. And also, no bad angles. Except maybe from below.` He swings to hang upside down on the branch. `Your chin looks a little wider and the lighting makes your—`

"Hey, stop being weird." Irynx scolds him.

"Stop being weird, Toffee!" Cor repeats.

`Someone say vibe?` Kukudh starts flicking the tabaxi's ears. `Haha, catto go brrr.` A glance from Sabrine; they stick their tongue out, turn into spider-crab form, and just chill on William's shoulder.

Will is unmoved by the familiar's shenanigans. He is calm in this chaos. Even with a dinosaur looking to put him in her mouth. 

Sabrine sighs. 'Apologies for Kukudh's… antics. They're somewhat restless.'

"Yep." Roy nods. "Standard Kukudh behavior. Don't worry, we know who's taking the next turn cleaning the Strider."

Without looking back up, Irynx adds, "Orphy will join them, too. Because I say so."

"Then I will join them as well!" Cheerfully says Will, and Ed just facepalms.

`Man, he's such a great person too!` Orphy squawks in exasperation.

"I just want to stay close to Ed, so I will do anything in my power to help their friends. That's not really being a great person. It's just being decent and considerate of others."

"Well, if you volunteer, welcome on board." Roy says, already having in mind how to split the job so Kukudh gets the worst part.

__**GOODBYE GRIMLOCK**__
Sabrine reaches out to scritch Grimmy behind the ears, casting Speak with Animals as she does so. 'Say hello to everyone for us, alright?'

Grimlock nods as she gets scritches under her chin. ||I can't take care of you anymore, my pets. Now you must go off on your own. But the people in Empire still need me.||

Roy joins in with Speak With Animals. "With you looking over the city, I'm sure we won't have anything to worry about."

Sabrine and Kukudh start to take on translator duty for those without animal-speaking capability.

"Thank you for being with us, Grim." Irynx places a palm over the side of Grimlock's head.

Ed is a snotty mess hearing about this, and is clinging to Grimmy's leg. Lilly also creeps up on Grimlock's other leg before returning to her flower pot. "I will come back to visit you then… I promise." They let go and look up at their huge friend. 

||I will come visit you first.|| Grimlock gives Ed one last lick, before lumbering off eastward. She looks back to the group one last time and roars loud and mighty, before continuing on her way secure in the knowledge that she will return.

__**BIRTHDAY**__
It was in Ed's worst interest to tell everyone of their birthday two days on the road from their last stop. Now they won't be able to get anything *fun* for a celebration. They'll probably only have barrels of water and two snarky familiars because of this mistake. Oh, and of course, William.

`Should've told us sooner. Well, guess we'll have to make do~` Kukudh swipes some leaves and sprinkles them over the birthday fluff.

    I had a long road ahead of me once the war was over. I was a mender; I was fighting in the war to rebuild what this city was meant to be about. In my first life I was building for the greatness of working men and women, we gave blood, sweat, and tears to get the roads laid out and the buildings stacked to the clouds. I died for that dream; my work was bastardized by business men hiring necromancers to keep the taskforce moving. At first, I was just another mindless builder. I saw the abuse the living workers were put through, almost like the top-hats wanted people to die just to make easier to manage workers. That’s what made me snap awake again. I came back full of rage; I beat back the taskmasters that would whip and try to break us. Andross Mortem may have been dead, but there was someone else standing in his Body, something else inside his Bones. That’s where you all met me.

----- scene 1 a walk down sesame sweet

“Good to see you come by Bones, so many have left for all over Arcania. How have things been in Kingsbridge?” It was always good to stop by Sesame Sweet to see Fuddles. Sonny has been doing a lot of planning and packing lately so I could only assume they were going to leave too. Thought it’s best to enjoy company while I have it, along with these shamrock cupcakes. 
“Things have been bustling. People got attracted to the new name on the umbral cup, but maybe I need to get a painter to put Gil on the front of it. They want to know who sandy is, givin me all kinds of funny looks.” I do my best to give her a smile, but I’m not the best at hiding what’s on my mind.
“Something wrong?” 
“I’ve just…thought a lot about Gil. And these headstones we all placed. The one in hampstead is part of what caused this mess, so somebody has to stick around and watch over them.” I could tell she understood, but looking to the room where sonny was working on maps for his next goal meant she knew she had a different road ahead. She got up to go talk with him while I habitually took out my matchless pipe. Good thing they invested in outdoor seating or else she’d have given me hell for smoking out the business. They finally came out after a couple minutes. Sonny looking spry as ever. “Howdy Sonny, heard you were planning quite a trip.” He wore a nice suit, changed to a traditional green for the vest, matched his skin now. His body may be a frog now but the green blood in his veins will never go away.

----- scene 2 back-alley bargain

“Yeah, but I always have time for my friends old man, the Mrs. tells me you were going to plant roots here in empire. We’re planning on living here. It’s just, there’s a lot out in different places that we can’t forget about. Anything we can do to help?” I Thought he’d never ask. 
“I’m looking after something important for Gil. I’ve made a good hiding spot for it and promised to keep it a secret, but to make sure it stays protected I had to find something solid, timeless.”
“Well, we got all kinds of magic in this town. Maybe before we leave, we can go through the library, or see if some of the cartels have something to help.”
“How about a bit of both?”
“Well, one thing at a time. Sis was always into magic and history, found a little bit of a tip involving a thingy. Thingies are usually pretty useful to start.”

There were a lot more guns than I expected. I knew Sonny was in cahoots with a lot of underhanded smugglers but I didn’t realize he heard a rumor about a local mafia like this. Some group invested in Ferrytown and Hampstead that had the leftovers of the lycanthrope torture supply from the gazette, among other magical goods like the ‘thing’ he mentioned. Why didn’t I follow Sonny behind those crates? This trolley doesn’t hold up against bullet fire. If that volt thrower guy got too close, I’d have nowhere to go. “I thought it too Bones, but in slang ‘it smells like a troll’ is code for not respecting someone and sending hitmen later!” That’s a lot of gunfire, oh boy. “You didn’t know.” Took me a moment to think, did sonny get shot or did he shoot someone? I had to move. The staff and twig were still saving my ass at least. Just gotta be faster than them. One hand using the staff, and one to outdo their mage stopper.
“I’ll keep that in mind!” That’s the volt thrower down, now where is- Ah, there she is. Damn that woman can pull weight, those are orcs. are they breathing? Well, they ain’t getting up that’s for sure.
“I got the, thing, sonny what did you say this was?”
“Ancient cryptid stone thingy, I don’t know it just sounded magic!”
“If we got it let’s get out of here you two. They ain’t slowing down.” There was no time for picks, this lock is breaking. The two horses would work for us. They really are a cute couple. A shame there wasn’t a sunset for him to ride her off to.
“We’ll uh, we’ll lead them this way don’t worry the library should help you.”
“Thanks, I owe you Both one, put it on my tab will ya?”

“These guys aren’t half as bad as swarms of redcoats. I could take this in my sleep” Fuddles sure could, I would hate to be on her bad side any day. Not as long as she has that axe, no, even without the axe she’s a force of nature.
“I just hope you’re still here when we come back, don’t go dying on us again!”
“Not planning on it!” Well, only one way to find out if this can help. One trip to the library, hopefully this can be a one book stop otherwise this could get dicey. At least those punks won’t follow me in there, I’d rather face redcoats than what they do to people causing a ruckus. This thing is pretty heavy so hopefully it’s useful.

----- scene 3 an avalanche of knowledge

Actually a little noisy in the library. Lots of footsteps trying to learn more about so much that happened near the end of the war. Months of research in here was rough but this is definitely getting somewhere. ‘Cryptids are attracted to historical events, a divination ability they have to just know when something memorable is going on. Still nothing about this thing Sonny acquired for me. ‘Cryptids are also known to be attracted to places and objects that have survived for long periods of time. They can sometimes be found protecting ancient sites or treasures that have been used in historical events. “hahhahhah, yes. I know all kinds of things about cryptids and magical items. But that’s a lot of very sensitive knowledge. “I reckon they wouldn’t be. I’m trying to find ways to protect something indefinitely. I got a bit of a passion project going on.”
“Passion, joy, excitement! That’s what we live for! When you find purpose it’s always good to make a plan and give it everything you got! It puts a smile on my face to see a friend of Gil’s trying to build on his legacy, it was always so sad before when he was a hero in death.”
“You knew sandy? How?”
“That’s a story for another day, and perhaps if you read enough BOOKS! You’ll come across the tale much like that vampire novel you’ve been reading. How is it by the way?”

That night you sleep really well. You dream of the river, and of some warm feeling coming from it. When you wake up, for the first time in a while, your mind is fully made up.

You died, back in Hampstead's winding alleys, when the fog was engulfing the borough. And then you woke up. Wait, what?

You look at your hands - your skin seems paler, dark blood vessels making a striking contrast. You move - your muscle memory seems intact and you're not tripping over your own feet, though it hurts slightly more than you're used to.
But it's still you, you didn't get turned into some... chimera abomination by that mad scientist you've heard lives around. But then, what happened? And what will happen if anyone finds you...?
You stick to going out only in the fog, at first, staying in an abandoned building any other time. It's easy enough to hide there, and the pigeons are at least good companionship. But then the borough burns, and the fog fades, and reconstruction begins. You start to venture out during the night, to find something, anything, you can use as food - not that you need to eat, but chewing things helps you stay sane - but often, you come back to whatever shelter in the rubble you've managed to piece together to find it cleared away, and multiple times you've been disturbed from your rest - not sleep, never sleep - by people approaching, and have had to scramble to find a new place before anyone finds you.
